touches.angle: Investment introduction to a founder. Reference the supplied source-backed signal and explain why it relates to the sender's stated research thesis. Say you are interested in learning more about the business and exploring a potential investment conversation. Ask whether they are open to a short call. Never imply a committed investment, claim fund affiliation, or invent credentials, check sizes, portfolio companies or traction. Do not mention job applications or attach a resume. Under 120 words.
Brief follow-up to the investment introduction. Revisit one supported detail without claiming new developments or inventing value to offer. Ask if a conversation would be useful. Under 60 words.
Brief investment follow-up. Ask one thoughtful question grounded in the supplied company context. Do not invent market facts or fundraising plans. Under 70 words.
Close the investment outreach politely. Say this is the last follow-up, leave the door open and do not pressure the founder. Under 50 words.
